name: Peapods Finance: Yoink's USDC-market exploit after the attacker's three failed attempts
race_type_reason: The attacker's three pair-2 attempts (blocks 22874007-09) had already landed and each reverted inside its try/catch; Yoink's tx (22874010 idx 0, 12 s later) made the same 42 state-changing calls (role-normalised, similarity 1.0, same 10M USDC Morpho loan, same swap sizes) and its borrow passed. No attacker tx is shown pending, and the attacker's calldata on the pre-Yoink state still reverts.
one_liner: After the attacker's pair-1 exploit (+78.19 ETH) and three reverted pair-2 attempts, Yoink replayed the same 42-call recipe one block later and took 174,258 USDC with an 11.49 ETH bribe; it returned 126,892 USDC (90% after cost). No pending attacker tx is shown.

trigger.note: Not a measured trigger. The most recent on-chain attacker pair-2 attempt before Yoink was 22874009 (12 s earlier, reverted internally). Auction timeline: first large bid (4.91 ETH, beaverbuild) 6.1 s after that block was sealed, so the trigger could be that tx or the bot's own watch of the Peapods pairs; unknown.

attacker_block_note: Last attacker pair-2 attempt (landed, reverted internally). Earlier success: pair 1 at 22873986 idx 4 (+78.1864 ETH), which Phalcon labels the 'Attack Transaction'.

loot.gross_loot_method: ETH-equivalent of 174,258.313813 USDC at the Yoink vault's own cost-recovery swap rate on 2025-07-10 (33,267.41 USDC -> 11.95248 ETH, tx 0x405e44f4, 3 min before the return); not a market oracle. The take itself is USDC.

captured_native.desc: borrowAsset on Peapods/Fraxlend pair 0xca1154bb (516,065.925 USDC borrowed, loan repaid inside the tx); 174,258.313813 USDC swept to the Yoink vault 0xc70f00cd

loot.loot_note: Scope is tx0. bot_net = gross (ETH-equivalent) - tx0 coinbase (11.4944) - gas (0.00379); priority fee 0 and no builder refund (block has 3 Yoink txs + the proposer payment). Coinbase paid by all three Yoink txs in the block is 11.9877 ETH (builder paid the proposer 12.4423); Yoink's own message says it paid 11.95248 ETH, which differs from the measured 11.9877 by 0.0352 ETH (unreconciled). tx1's arbitrage profit is not credited here.

fate.returned_to: Peapods team address 0x21fe3e26e824783ca7e374355a8d30ae8bbf6e37 (the address that messaged the bot and attacker)
fate.returned_desc: 2025-07-10: Peapods offered a 10% white-hat bounty (tx 0xf24a9464, block 22888679). The Yoink vault replied on chain (tx 0xa1856637): 'Frontran 0x277da2D1ce5601c0f0133515c19DA314fc52a846 here. Unfortunately had to pay 11.95248 Eth to win the block, so will remove that first ...'. It sold 33,267.41 USDC for 11.95248 ETH (cost recovery), then sent 126,891.81 USDC to the team (tx 0xe64f202c, block 22889167) = exactly 90% of the remaining 140,990.91 USDC; 72.8% of the gross take. returned_*_eth are ETH-equivalents at the cost-recovery swap rate; the real return was in USDC (returned_usdc).
fate.bounty_desc: 14,099.10 USDC (10% of the post-cost amount) kept, sold for 4.4977981980052295 ETH on 2025-07-16 (tx 0x2a6f4354)
fate.public_statement: on-chain messages: Peapods (tx 0xf24a9464, 0xf051e900, thanks 0xd49d8e52) and the Yoink vault reply (0xa1856637); BlockSec/Phalcon via Quadriga calls tx0 'Second Transaction Which Was Front-run'.
fate.return_status_rule: returned = everything went back to the victim side except a bounty the victim agreed to or offered; partial = some came back, otherwise; none = known zero within the documented search window; unknown = unresolved

rawref_gaps.why: neither side's txs are in mempool-dumpster; no trigger measured
pair-2 borrowAsset reverts with custom error 0xed27783c(uint256) (arg = borrow + 1 unit); the attacker contract and the pair's error are not decoded from verified source
USDC amounts converted at the vault's own swap rate, not a market price feed

discrepancies: Phalcon/BlockSec (via Quadriga) and Peapods' thank-you message say Yoink front-ran the attacker's second attempt; on-chain the attacker's pair-2 attempts had already landed and failed before Yoink's tx, and none of them was pre-empted.
Press loss figure (~$200k, ~78 ETH) is the attacker's pair-1 take; Yoink's 174,258 USDC from pair 2 is additional (lender vault 0x3717e340 fell from 463,970.31 to 115,704.36 USDC in this block).
Yoink's stated cost of winning the block (11.95248 ETH) vs measured coinbase total 11.98767 ETH.
evidence_notes: incidents/peapods-2025/call_diff.json: the attacker's blocks 22874007/08/09 pair-2 callbacks equal Yoink's 42 state-changing calls role-for-role (ratio 1.0); borrow sizes differ at the 7th digit (attacker 516,041.99 / 516,065.93 / 516,041.99 vs Yoink 516,065.925 USDC).

debug_traceCall of the attacker's calldata on the state after 22874009 (just before Yoink) still reverts in borrowAsset; on the state after 22874010 and 22874014 it stops at 'zero token'. So Yoink did exhaust the opportunity, but the attacker's own tx was not shown to succeed without it.
Auction (slot 12095680): winning builder 'I can haz block?' via Flashbots, 12.4423 ETH to the proposer; first >4 ETH bid appears 6.1 s after the attacker's last attempt block.
Bribe rule: msg.value 114944269 (>=1000) is a fixed bribe of v x 1e11 wei = 11.4944269 ETH, equal to the coinbase transfer in the trace.

name: Peapods Finance: Yoink sweeps a user's stranded 8,957 USDC from the LeverageManager (2025-10-09)
race_type_reason: A user's removeLeverage tx (block 23540172) left 8,957.748779 USDC in the LeverageManager. Yoink swept it 10 blocks (~2 min) later via a different function, first and alone; there is no attacker and no pending tx to beat. It is a first-sweeper case with a good-faith return, not a race.
one_liner: A user's removeLeverage left 8,957.75 USDC in the Peapods LeverageManager; Yoink swept it 10 blocks later (idx 0, 1.80 ETH coinbase, builder refund 1.57 ETH) and returned 1.4163 ETH, 90% of its net. No attacker; not a race.

attacker.none_reason: No attacker: the leftover was created by an ordinary user's removeLeverage tx; Yoink was the first to sweep it.

attacker_block_note: No attacker; the user tx that stranded the funds is block 23540172.

loot.gross_loot_method: ETH received by the Yoink contract in the tx trace (2.040570) minus the 0.233938 ETH the tx itself wrapped into WETH.deposit; the take is the 8,957.748779 USDC left in the LeverageManager, sold inside the tx

captured_native.desc: USDC balance of LeverageManager 0x4e6ef371 before the tx (eth_call balanceOf at block 23540181), 0 after

loot.loot_note: Scope is the single Yoink tx. bot_net = gross - coinbase + builder refund - gas (0.000616 ETH at 0.294285336 gwei). The block has 3 txs: Yoink idx 0, the builder's refund idx 1 (1.5725 ETH to the bot contract) and the proposer payment idx 2. Coinbase msg.value 999 (per mille rule) = 1.8048 ETH; the refund returned most of it, so the bot ended with 1.5736 ETH. Gross is the measured ETH received by the bot contract in the trace (2.0406) minus the 0.2339 ETH the tx wrapped into WETH; Yoink's own return (1.416285 ETH) is exactly 90% of the net computed this way, which supports treating the wrapped amount as a cost. The ETH value of the 8,957.75 USDC is not separately priced.

Yoink returned 1.416285 ETH at 17:46:23Z (tx 0xcd6d475f, block 23541758) with the message 'Returning profits minus 10% bounty': 90.00% of its 1.5736 ETH net.
